text:
sam: Quick follow-up on the autoscaler RFC — proposal for a hybrid cold-start budget per-tenant. Idea: allocate small "cold_budget" tokens that can be spent to prewarm slots proactively (predictive) and also as emergency one-off bursts (reactive).

maria: Sounds interesting. How is cold_budget different from existing burst credits? :thinking:

sam: TL;DR: burst credits are generic throughput cushions. cold_budget is explicitly for warmup/cold-start actions (start VM, pull weights, load model into GPU). Separate accounting prevents burst credits being eaten by sustained traffic.

alex: Can you sketch config?

sam: Sure — thinking of a user-facing policy fragment:```yaml
autoscaling:
  strategy: hybrid
  cold_budget:
    initial: 5      # tokens at tenant creation
    refill_rate: 1/hour
    max_tokens: 20
  predictive:
    lookback: 10m
    model: simple-exponential
  reactive:
    emergency_threshold_ms: 300  # if tail lat > this, allow spend
```

jen: Who pays for the prewarm GPU runtime while it's being pulled? We need a chargeback model or else infra will eat costs.

sam: Good point. Proposal: distinguish two charges — prewarm_cost and runtime_cost. Prewarm_cost is billed as a fixed short-term startup delta against cold_budget spend; if prewarm was predictive (scheduled), charge goes to tenant; if we mispredicted and evict, refund partial credit.

kai: Refunds are tricky operationally. Can we simplify: predictive prewarms are reservations (tenant pays), reactive prewarms are subsidized up to N tokens per month (trial/SLAs), anything over gets billed?

maria: That feels reasonable. We should tie subsidized tokens to plan/tier. Also need operator-side guardrails so a noisy tenant can't drain cluster capacity via predictive scheduling.

alex: Operator handshake idea: the operator API should expose AdmitIntent objects with fields: required_gpu_count, cold_budget_spend_estimate, prewarm_expected_duration. The operator can reject or delay with reasons (capacity, safety). Example:```json
{"tenant":"t-123","required_gpu_count":2,"cold_budget_spend_estimate":3,"prewarm_expected_duration_s":120}
```

sam: Exactly. That keeps the orchestration boundary clear: control-plane requests -> operator admits or suggests alternate (defer to preemptible nodes or queue).

jen: Observability: we need metrics: cold_budget_spent_total, cold_budget_refills, predictive_prewarms, reactive_prewarms, prewarm_failures. Also an alert when predictive_prewarms > 50% of available headroom.

kai: For rollout, start with a tenant opt-in and a small sample pool. Also add a kill-switch at operator to force-disable predictive spends cluster-wide.

maria: Policy compatibility: this must play nicely with dedicated pools that have reserved nodes vs. burst lanes on shared infra. Suggest mapping cold_budget semantics to pool types: reserved pools always honor predictive prewarms; shared pools require operator approval and have stricter subsidized caps.

alex: Edge cases: model switch during prewarm (different weights) — prewarm might fail or be wasted. Proposal: attach an "expected_model_hash" to AdmitIntent; operator can abort if mismatch.

sam: Nice. That helps avoid wasted bandwidth. Also include TTL on prewarm leases so stale prewarms free up after X seconds.

infra-bot: deployment-note: tested config schema in staging. predictive lookback component rolled to canary cluster (canary=1/10 tenants) — no regressions observed.

jen: One more ops ask — add dry-run flag to the admit API so we can simulate cost/impact without actually provisioning GPUs. Useful for canary checks.

sam: Agreed. We'll add admit?dry_run=true semantics and return an estimated sidecar: {"estimated_cost","prewarm_time_s","rejected_reasons"}.

maria: Next steps: write short RFC addendum with config schema, operator AdmitIntent proto, metrics dashboard, and rollout plan (opt-in -> canary -> tiered enable). I'll draft and ping folks for review.

alex: 👍 please include sample PromQL queries and the dry-run API example.

sam: Thanks all — I'll put a sketch PR up for the addendum today. :rocket:
